title: Earith (mid-air collision) Stirling Memorial

external_narratives.summary: Memorial page for Stirling W7467 of 7 Squadron. On 17 January 1942, the Stirling was rammed by Hurricane V6865 from 56 OTU during a mock attack north of Earith Bridge. The Stirling dived into the ground to a depth of 15 feet at Haddenham Drain. All eight Stirling crew and the Hurricane pilot killed.
key_details: Hurricane carried out mock attack on Stirling
Stirling buried 15 feet deep at Haddenham Drain
Remains of Sgt Mankelow never recovered
Memorial erected 1999 by Parish Council and 7 Squadron Association

memorial_details:
Name: Short Stirling W7467
Type: Board / Plaque / Tablet
Description: Black granite tablet with incised inscription and names finished in gilt, set flush into a purpose-built brick wall. Coloured squadron badge at top of tablet. The whole memorial stands within an enclosed roadside corner plot.
Inscription: On 17th January 1942 Stirling Aircraft W7467, of 7 Squadron, RAF, / flying from RAF Oakington, collided with a Hurricane Aircraft of No 56 OTU and crashed 1.5 miles north of Earith / All crew members were killed / (7 Names) / These received Christian Burials at Cambridge, Dundee and Thurrock / Walter Mankelow, RAFVR, Air-Gnr. and James McCarley, RAFVR, Air-Gnr. / are remembered on the Royal Air Force Memorial at Runnymede, / as having no known grave / The people of Earith, 7 Squadron Association and this Stone remember them / Per Diem Per Noctem / 7th November 1999
Location: East of village memorial on corner plot 30 metres just over River Delph roadbridge, Air Crash Memorial A1123 Road Earith Huntingdon Cambridgeshire PE28 3PT England
Grid Ref: TL 38927 74836
Coordinates: 52.353991037931,0.038452088088
Photos: https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/73/370/large_p1010407_1_0.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/170/716/large_46478.jpg

Charles left no stone unturned approaching the Home Office, the Commonwealth War Graves Commission, AHB (RAF) the County Police Headquarters in Cambridgeshire, RAF Innsworth, Cambridgeshire County Council, Seven Squadron Association and all local cemeteries and Parish Councils, all to no avail.

In 1999 a Memorial was erected

Remains Discovery (1959): Work on Haddenham Drain uncovered further remains, assumed to be those of the lost airman. No identity could be established and the bones were disposed of by the police.
narrative: On 17 January 1942, Stirling W7467 of 7 Squadron departed RAF Oakington when it was struck by a Hurricane from 56 Operational Training Unit just north of Earith Bridge, Cambridgeshire. The collision sent the Stirling diving into the ground to a depth of fifteen feet at the Haddenham Drain, where it burned for several days before the crater filled with water. All eight crew aboard the Stirling were killed, as was the Hurricane pilot, Pilot Officer Browne — nine dead in total. The remains of Sergeant McCarley and Sergeant Walter Mankelow could not be recovered from the flooded crater. In 1959, further remains were found during drainage work but could not be identified, and no relatives were contacted. The fate of Sergeant Mankelow's remains was never formally resolved.
